subject: biology
title: Plant Biology (HL) Adventure 2: Phloem and translocation
welcome_lead: Today you'll load sucrose and watch phloem flow source-to-sink.
meta_desc: Biology HL — phloem, sieve tubes, companion cells, translocation, mass flow hypothesis.
final_note: You learned phloem moves sucrose from source to sink via mass flow, loaded by H⁺-coupled active transport, hydrostatic pressure does the rest.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Phloem is living tissue made of:

- Sieve tube elements — long cells with perforated sieve plates, lacking nuclei.
- Companion cells — adjacent, with mitochondria, support sieve tubes via plasmodesmata.

Münch (1930):

1. Companion cells use H⁺-ATPase + sucrose-H⁺ cotransport to load sucrose into sieve tube (active).
2. Water follows by osmosis → high turgor at source.
3. Hydrostatic pressure pushes solution to sink.
4. At sink, sucrose unloaded → water exits → low pressure.

Flow rate: up to 1 m h⁻¹.

Aphid stylet experiment — aphids pierce one sieve tube, sap exudes under pressure even after aphid removed → proves positive pressure.

Radioactive ¹⁴C tracers show sucrose flow direction matches source-sink prediction.

However, lateral movement and bidirectional flow under some conditions complicate the simple model — nature of science: theories are continually refined.
